land.text: Kāśī, conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala c. 600 BCE

predecessors.note: Kāśī joins Kosala in the founding year of this dossier; Kosala's own core is Awadh.

land.text: Kosala with Kāśī: 'finally defeated and absorbed into the Magadha kingdom in the 5th century BCE'; infobox 'Succeeded by: Magadha'. Land as in the -600 keyframe: Awadh cut to the page's Gomti, Sarpika and Sadanira bounds, with Kāśī, minus Vatsa

successors.note: Cliopatria's Haryanka row (-450..-405, 335,215 km2, bbox 80.90-88.61E) swells over this ground in -450.

capitals.name: Shravasti (Savatthi)
capitals.note: 'Shravasti is recorded as the capital of Kosala during the Mahajanapada period (6th-5th centuries BCE)'. The infobox gives 'Ayodhya and Shravasti of Uttar Kosala' and the Mahajanapadas page 'its capital at Ayodhya' (Saketa); Ayodhya (82.20E 26.80N) is the older and later capital. Shravasti is not in the gazetteer.

correction.text: 'Kosala was bounded by the Gomti River in the west, Sarpika River in the south, Sadanira in the east which separated it from Videha, and the Nepal Hills in the north'; 'It roughly corresponds to modern-day Awadh region'; with Kāśī, conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala c. 600 BCE (Kāśī page infobox), and without Cliopatria's Vatsa disc, which lies south of the Sarpika

keyframe_review.note: The 4,990 km2 disc (centroid 81.84E 27.16N, between Ayodhya and Shravasti) is a core of the two capitals. The page gives no area; it says Kosala 'roughly corresponds to modern-day Awadh region' and 'was bounded by the Gomti River in the west, Sarpika River in the south, Sadanira in the east which separated it from Videha, and the Nepal Hills in the north'. The gazetteer's Awadh (469 cells, about 117,600 km2, 24 times the disc; Uttar Pradesh within 79.5-83.5E, 25.4-28.5N) runs west of the Gomti and south across the Ganga and the Yamuna. The first version of this correction used it whole and so took in 14 of the 15 cells of Cliopatria's Vatsa disc (Kausambi, -600..-451) and about 57 cells (about 14,400 km2) of the Cedi dossier's corrected land (Banda 90 km + Rewa 50 km). Corrected after the adversarial review of 2026-10-18: Awadh intersected with a polygon (80.9-83.5E; south edge 26.2N at 80.9E, 26.0N at 81.6E, 25.9N from 82.4E; north edge 28.5N) that follows the Gomti on the west and the Sarpika on the south, united with Cliopatria's Kāśī disc and cut by Cliopatria's Vatsa disc: 231 cells, about 57,800 km2 (11.6 times the disc), one piece, 1.1 km from Shravasti; 0 cells shared with Vatsa, the Cedi dossier's land, Malla, Pañcāla, Anga, Gandhāra or Aśmaka. It borders Vatsa on the south-west (5 Vatsa cells touch it), contains Kāśī on the south, lies about 35 km (nearest cell centres) from the Malla disc on the east and 137 km from Pañcāla on the west. The Nepal side of the Terai is not drawn: the gazetteer's Awadh stops at the Indian border, so the page's Nepal Hills edge is approximated by it. Kāśī is added from -600 (Kāśī infobox 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE'; the Kosala page has 'By the 5th century BCE under the reign of King Mahakosala, the neighboring Kingdom of Kashi had been conquered'), which Cliopatria draws as a separate state.

correction.text: 'Kosala was bounded by the Gomti River in the west, Sarpika River in the south, Sadanira in the east which separated it from Videha, and the Nepal Hills in the north'; 'It roughly corresponds to modern-day Awadh region'; with Kāśī, conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala c. 600 BCE (Kāśī page infobox), and without Cliopatria's Vatsa disc, which lies south of the Sarpika

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria repeats the disc for -480..-451. The page adds nothing that moves the line in these years: Viḍūḍabha's absorption of the Kālāmas and of the Sakya and Koliya republics ('Shortly after the Buddha's death') has no year on the page, so the shape is the -600 correction carried through to the end. The Shakya page (opened in the repair) dates Viḍūḍabha's conquest of the Sakya and Koliya states only 'c. 5th century BCE'; they lie in the Terai, mostly beyond the drawn land, and have no dossier, so the shape does not move.

region.text: 'Kosala was bounded by the Gomti River in the west, Sarpika River in the south, Sadanira in the east which separated it from Videha, and the Nepal Hills in the north'; 'It roughly corresponds to modern-day Awadh region'; Kosala without Kāśī (gained next) and without Cliopatria's Vatsa disc

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Kosala, ruled from Shravasti, stands on Awadh as one of the four powers of the north. The infobox has 'Established: c. 7th century BCE', and 'About 500 BCE, during the reign of King Prasenajit (Pasenadi)' it 'was regarded as one of the four powers of the north'; -600 is Cliopatria's start, so the year is a bridge.

region.text: Kāśī, conquered by Kosala under Kaṃsa

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Kaṃsa of Kosala conquers Kāśī. Kāśī infobox 'Conquered by Kaṃsa of Kosala: c. 600 BCE'; 'Kāśī was finally conquered for good by Kosala under the latter's king Kaṃsa'. The Kosala page's lead says only 'It annexed the powerful kingdom of Kashi' (no date) and its history section 'By the 5th century BCE under the reign of King Mahakosala, the neighboring Kingdom of Kashi had been conquered'; the Mahajanapadas page 'during Buddha's time'. The year is the Kāśī infobox's, the exact date uncertain.

region.text: all of Kosala, Kāśī included, absorbed into Magadha (land as in the -600 keyframe: Awadh cut to the page's bounds, with Kāśī, minus Vatsa)

ledger.note: c. 451 BCE: Magadha absorbs Kosala after Ajatashatru kills Viḍūḍabha. 'it was finally defeated and absorbed into the Magadha kingdom in the 5th century BCE'; 'Viḍūḍabha was defeated and killed by the Māgadhī king Ajātasattu'; infobox 'Disestablished: c. 5th century BCE'. The page gives the century only; -451 is Cliopatria's last year (its Haryanka row swells in -450). By the Mahavamsa chronology on the Haryanka page Ajatashatru reigned 493-462, which would put the fall before -462. The Ajatashatru page (opened in the repair) is also silent on the year: 'Ajatashatru occupied Kashi and captured the smaller kingdoms', the Jain account 'Ajatashatru not only conquered Vaishali but also Kasi-Kosala', and the Kashi dispute 'ended in a peace treaty in which Prasenajit married his daughter Vajira to him'; it dates his reign 493-461 BCE (long chronology) or c. 405-373 BCE (Sarao). The Shakya page (also opened) has the Sakya and Koliya states 'Conquered by Viḍūḍabha of Kosala: c. 5th century BCE', after 'Shortly after the Buddha's death'; they are not drawn (Terai, no dossier).

wars.name: Kosala-Magadha war over the Kāśī village
wars.outcome: Pasenadi 'revoked his rights over the village in Kāśī, after which a war between Kosala and Magadha ensued'; he then 'gave him in marriage his daughter Vajirā, to whom he gifted the village in Kāśī, and restored him to his throne.'
wars.note: Undated on the page. The span is Ajatashatru's reign by the Mahavamsa chronology on the Haryanka page (493-462; its infobox says 492-460). The village (a dowry of Bimbisara's marriage to Kosala Devi, revenue of 'a hundred thousand') is below a cell, so no zone. The Ajatashatru page, opened in the repair, also gives no year: the Kashi dispute 'led to a war between Magadha and Kosala' and 'ended in a peace treaty in which Prasenajit married his daughter Vajira to him'.

wars.name: Magadhan conquest of Kosala (Ajatashatru and Viḍūḍabha)
wars.outcome: 'Viḍūḍabha was defeated and killed by the Māgadhī king Ajātasattu' and Kosala was 'absorbed into the Magadha kingdom in the 5th century BCE'.
wars.note: No battle, front or year is on the pages: the span runs from Ajatashatru's accession (Haryanka page 493/492) to Cliopatria's last Kosala year, and the whole land passes at the dissolve event. Under Mahapadma Nanda 'Koshala rebelled but the rebellion was put down' (Kosala page, c. 345 BCE, outside this dossier).

certainty.note: Only rivers bound the kingdom (Gomti, Sarpika, Sadanira) and the Nepal hills; the Kāśī frontier, the Sakya and Koliya republics and Videha are all approximate.

notes: Both Cliopatria shapes are the same 4,990 km2 disc between Ayodhya and Shravasti; they are corrected to Awadh (the page's own word) cut to the page's bounds (Gomti, Sarpika, Sadanira) by a polygon, plus Kāśī from -600 and minus Cliopatria's Vatsa disc (the gazetteer's Awadh is a 117,600 km2 rectangle of Uttar Pradesh that swallowed Vatsa and 57 cells of the Cedi dossier's land; fixed after the adversarial review of 2026-10-18, 231 cells, about 57,800 km2), because the Kāśī page makes Kosala the conqueror of Kāśī c. 600 BCE while Cliopatria keeps Kāśī separate to -451 (see the Kāśī dossier; if the reviewer keeps Kāśī alive, delete the Kāśī union from the Kosala shapes and the -600 gain). Not in the ledger because no year can be drawn from the pages: Viḍūḍabha's annexation of the Kālāmas and of the Sakya and Koliya republics ('Shortly after the Buddha's death', Kosala page; Kapilavastu is not named; the Shakya page, opened in the repair, gives only the infobox 'c. 5th century BCE'), and Mallakas who 'helped Pasenadi's son Viḍūḍabha usurp the throne'; the Sakya, Koliya and Kalama republics have no dossier (counterparts_needing_dossiers). The end is the 5th century BCE on every page; -451 is Cliopatria's and conflicts with the Mahavamsa chronology (Ajatashatru d. 462) and Sarao's (Ajatashatru 405-373): the Haryanka dossier should settle it. Pages: Kosala, Kāśī, the shared Mahajanapadas page, and the Haryanka page for Ajatashatru's reign (budget 1-2 per state; two pages shared with sibling dossiers). Gazetteer lacks: Shravasti (place, 27.52N 82.05E, Sahet-Mahet), used only in a capital entry.
